text_en: Ancestry.com is a leading American genealogy company that has revolutionized the way people explore their family history. Founded in 1983 by John Sittner and originally known as The Generations Network, the company operates a vast network of websites, including its flagship platform Ancestry.com, as well as FamilySearch, Find A Grave, and Fold3. These platforms provide users with access to billions of historical records, such as census data, military records, immigration documents, and even DNA testing services through AncestryDNA. By leveraging advanced search algorithms and crowdsourced data, Ancestry.com has democratized genealogical research, making it accessible to millions of users worldwide. The company’s database is continuously updated with new records, ensuring that families can trace their roots back centuries. Ancestry.com was acquired by private equity firm Blackstone in 2020 for $4.7 billion, highlighting its immense value and influence in the genealogy industry. Today, it remains the largest for-profit genealogy company globally, shaping how people connect with their past.
text_fr: Ancestry.com est une entreprise américaine spécialisée dans la généalogie, fondée en 1983 par John Sittner sous le nom de *The Generations Network*. Elle est devenue un acteur incontournable dans l’exploration des origines familiales, proposant une plateforme en ligne riche en archives historiques. Son site phare, Ancestry.com, ainsi que des services comme *FamilySearch*, *Find A Grave* et *Fold3*, offrent aux utilisateurs un accès à des milliards de documents : recensements, registres militaires, actes d’immigration, et même des tests ADN via *AncestryDNA*. Grâce à des algorithmes de recherche performants et des contributions communautaires, Ancestry.com a rendu la généalogie accessible au grand public, permettant à des millions de personnes de retracer leur histoire sur plusieurs siècles. En 2020, le groupe Blackstone a racheté Ancestry pour 4,7 milliards de dollars, confirmant son statut de géant du secteur. Aujourd’hui, l’entreprise reste la plus grande société privée de généalogie au monde, influençant durablement la manière dont les individus se reconnectent à leur passé.
